Does the home microbiome relate to asthma?

Household dust connects land use, indoor microbes and childhood respiratory health.

Our everyday environments are designed. What can this published study actually tell us about their relationship with human health and the brain?

The study

Researchers compared microbial communities in HVAC dust from rural and urban homes and assessed nearby land use and childhood asthma status.

The findings

Bacterial and fungal diversity varied with environmental context; microbial profiles also differed between homes with and without childhood asthma. The study does not establish that a specific microbe caused asthma.

What this means for architecture

Ventilation, surroundings and materials may alter microbial exposure, but design prescriptions need intervention evidence.

Conclusion

The evidence points to an important research question, not a universal design rule. Better controlled and longer-term studies are needed.

Building and Environment study (2024)

Microbial communities in rural and urban homes and their relationship to surrounding land use, household characteristics, and asthma status. Building and Environment 266, 112014
